content:
This is definitely a clash, but if you would prefer to keep it as a classic puzzle only minor adjustments would be needed.
Giving and requesting extra information is an easy way to make it harder. For example:
You could give the sales with an item name and time, and have the coder find the time of the sale that reached the revenue target and/or the percentage of total sales that consisted of that item. Something along those lines.

General
* This seems too easy as a puzzle. Please re-create the contribution as a clash of code.

Formatting
* Please study the formatting syntax described on this page: https://www.codingame.com/playgrounds/40701/help-center/statement , and format your statement properly by following the example there (e.g. variables [[N]] and [[M]], constant {{IMPOSSIBLE}}, line numbers in bold <<Line 1>>).

Constraints
* Please use upper bounds that are closer to the values used in the actual cases.

Cases
* Every test and its corresponding validator should cover the same scenario, but with slightly different inputs and outputs (except in the case of IMPOSSIBLE).

Thanks.

Alternatively, consider removing the constraint whereby the sales must be processed in the order they occurred. The new challenge (slightly harder, probably suitable for both clash and puzzle) is to figure out the minimum number of sales required to reach/exceed the revenue target.

Also, if this were to be a puzzle, please generate more cases where the number of sales (M) is large (~1000, as you suggest). Thank you!
